text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Salaries in Croatia will rise by six percent due to tax reduction in the following year. Public services and state administration will enjoy 11 percent increase.

- Countrywide elections scheduled for March will include the last rebel Serb enclave of East Slavonia for the first time in fivbe years, president Tudjman and U.N. administrator in the enclave Jacques Klein said in a meeting.
- Some 2,000 homes in East Slavonia will be repaired next year offering most displaced persons better homes than what they had before the war, says reconstruction minister Jure Radic.
- Overhaul of Rijecka Banka, one of the biggest ailing banks burdening Croatian financial market has been completed without mass layoffs, says prime minister Zlatko Matesa.
- Pensions are beginning to catch up with salaries. Government announced ten percent increase from January.
- Government completes rehabilitation programmes for 16 companies.
- President Tudjman's health is under control, says health minister Andrija Hebrang following a surgery for alleged stomach cancer in the U.S. last month.
- Croatian economy is in recession, say critics of the specialised weekly Ekonomija, despite official government line claiming it was recovering.
- Two blue chips: drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka sealed the current year by hitting record high prices on the stock market.
- Textile company Heruc signes a licence contract with the Italian company Enrico Coveri. Products with Coveri name will be sold in central and eastern Europe.
- Freak snow blizzard along most of the Adriatic coast caused traffic problems as drivers are unused to such weather conditions.
- Aluminium firm TLM in Sibenik escaped banktrupcy as government made plans for an overhaul, but restructuring and privatisation await the former loss making giant. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
